item.title: The Shadow Door
item.content:encoded: The transitions between "base reality" and "storybook reality" are too sudden and awkwardly placed. How does this boy survive being eaten by his bed-turned-monster mouth? How ans why does the father disappear after his son esscapes? And how can s favorite adventure tale that's existed for decades suddenly act anomolous, without developing s reputation as "the book you'd better not read to kids…especially not by reassuring the kids that it's only fiction"? (Shades of SCP-1241 here…)

item.title: The Huron Carol
item.content:encoded:
I hope that you've enjoyed my tale
I hope it finds you well;
If I write one more verse of rhyme
I think I'll go to hell;
But honestly it's been a slice,
I hope your holidays are nice;
Don't forget, you're the best,
Keep hanging on;
Please remain in quarantine!

I've been made to feel very welcome during this, my first year on the site. Looking forward to continuing to get to know you all better, and no matter what this time of the year means to you — I'm an atheist, so it means family, food and commercialism to me, and so I'm staying in with my dad, eating whatever he got from the grocery store last week, and not spreading disease like a goddamn sollipsist — I hope it works out for you in some respect.

Here's to next year.

Citation: The "Huron Carol" was written in Wyandot in 1642 by Jean de Brébeuf; using his melody (which was adapted from a French folk tune) Jesse Edgar Middleton wrote the English lyrics in 1926, and they entered the public domain in 2011. (Music copyright lengths are fucking stupid.) My version is, obviously, my own.

All images are the author's, released under CC 3.0.

item.title: SCP-5266
item.content:encoded:
Juxtaposition~!

Thanks to Mooagain, RadioactiveRADS, Cope, Topazshadow, Alongname, and Jabobai for critique and feedback. They helped me refine the idea and come up with the final log. The picture is mine, of me body-slamming the floor out of commitment to art.

Anyways, always remember: No matter how seriously the Foundation or anyone else takes itself, it is still always possible for something ridiculous to come out of nowhere to dunk on you. Because anomalies are, by their very definition, weird. And I like weird. Not to mention how fun it was trying to write action sequences set to Village People music, I hope I was able to translate timing-based jokes to a written format well enough.

I hope you all enjoy!

item.title: Hear those Slay-Bells ring-a-ling
item.content:encoded:
And here we have my first foray into tale writing and into horror.

Admittedly, the length kind of got away from me, but overall I like it. Although I think that while I was aiming for 'unknowable supernatural horror', I may have strayed closer to 'generic slasher' but… hey, if movies like "Black Christmas" can become cult classics, maybe this can too?

I would also like to give a special thanks to SCP-4666 for being so goddamn creepy.

item.title: SCP-0110-J
item.content:encoded:
I am not sorry. The existence of this article is solely SCPD’s fault. All of the needed citation is provided in the Ayers Infomodule.

Edit: Alright, so I suppose this gets comments gets a bunch of new words now that I woke up. I think I should explain what the hell this is - two months ago, I said on SCPD that if SCP-5464 somehow reaches +100, I will write something whilst drunk, similarly to what PeppersGhost did with SCP-3943 after winning the SCP-4000 Contest. People only encouraged me of course. However, since I had no such beverages at my disposal, I thought that sleep deprivation is a good substitute. This is the product of that challenge.

Edit 2: One more thing - I don’t actually hate Esoteric Object Classes. Whilst I don’t personally use them, I don’t mind them. It’s just a joke.
